THE THEME OF THIS ANNUAL REPORT 
ADVANCING THE SCIENCE OF PROGRESS 
REFLECTS NOT JUST WHAT WE DO, 
BUT WHO WE ARE.
EVERY MOLECULE  
THAT REACHES A PATIENT BEGINS 
WITH A QUESTION. AT COHANCE, 
WE EXIST TO ANSWER IT.
Chemistry is the oldest language of medicine. Long before biologics, 
before targeted oncology, before the era of precision therapeutics, 
chemists were the first problem-solvers of human health - working step 
by deliberate step, navigating the infinite complexity of molecular space, 
to construct compounds capable of extending and improving lives.
At Cohance Lifesciences, we have never left that bench. We have 
simply built more sophisticated tools around it - and surrounded it 
with the most demanding and most forward-looking pharmaceutical 
partnerships in the world.
We are a science-led enterprise that sits at the precise intersection 
of pharmaceutical innovation and global healthcare delivery. Every 
complex synthesis we execute, every novel modality platform we build, 
every innovator relationship we deepen - each is an act of advancing 
the science upon which the next generation of medicine depends.

THE END   
OF PIECEMEAL
For decades, the global pharmaceutical outsourcing model operated on a simple 
premise: break the value chain into discrete tasks, assign each to the lowest-
cost qualified provider, and manage the interfaces. It worked - until the science 
outgrew the model.
Today’s most promising therapeutic modalities - antibody-drug conjugates, 
oligonucleotides, precision biologics - are not simple molecules manufactured 
through linear sequences. They are convergent systems, where payload chemistry, 
linker design, bioconjugation, analytical characterisation, biological evaluation 
and process scale-up are not separate workstreams but interdependent scientific 
decisions. A change in linker architecture reshapes conjugation strategy. A shift in 
payload potency redefines containment requirements. An analytical finding at the 
bench can redirect a programme months before it reaches the clinic.
Cohance Lifesciences Limited
4
=== page 8 ===
In this environment, every handoff between vendors 
is a timeline risk, a quality risk and a knowledge 
discontinuity. Every transfer of technology from one 
partner to another is a transfer of institutional memory 
that the next partner must rebuild from scratch.
The world’s leading innovators have recognised this. 
Outsourcing is no longer a procurement exercise. It 
is a scientific partnership decision. And the partners 
they are choosing are those who can hold the entire 
chain — from molecular design through clinical-stage 
manufacture — under one roof, one quality system and 
one programme governance.
Leading innovators increasingly require partners who 
can connect scientific decisions across the development 
pathway. This calls for coordinated programme 
governance, continuous knowledge transfer and 
consistent quality standards across specialised 
capabilities—from molecular design and process 
development to clinical and commercial supply.
The opportunity is therefore concentrating in platforms 
that combine scientific depth with connected execution, 
rather than in providers offering isolated capacity.
Annual Report 2025-26Corporate Overview

=== page 9 ===
OUR INTEGRATED   
ADC PLATFORM
THE STORY
Some of the most advanced cancer treatments available today work by 
combining two things: an antibody that finds the tumour, and a potent 
drug that destroys it. These are called antibody-drug conjugates — therapies 
designed to deliver medicine directly to the disease, sparing healthy tissue the 
damage that conventional chemotherapy inflicts.
The science behind them is extraordinary. But so is the manufacturing 
challenge. Building one of these therapies requires deep expertise in at least 
half a dozen disciplines — from creating the potent drug molecule, to designing 
the chemical link that attaches it to the antibody, to joining them together 
under conditions so controlled that even trace impurities are unacceptable.
Until recently, pharmaceutical companies developing these therapies had no 
choice but to divide this work among five, six, sometimes seven different 
specialist providers — coordinating across time zones, quality systems and 
competing priorities. Every transfer from one provider to the next risked delay, 
information loss and quality variation.
Cohance connects the specialist capabilities required across this 
development chain — from payload-linker chemistry and high-containment 
process development to bioconjugation, analytical characterisation and clinical-
stage supply. By coordinating these activities across the platform, scientific 
learning can remain with the programme as it advances.
Cohance Lifesciences Limited
6
=== page 10 ===
THE SCIENCE
Antibody-drug conjugates are convergent systems requiring 
mastery across three distinct chemistries: antibody 
engineering, cytotoxic payload-linker synthesis and bioconjugation. 
Twenty-two ADCs have received regulatory approval globally, 
fourteen from the US FDA. Approved ADC therapies generated 
approximately US$ 16 billion in global sales in 2025, projected to 
surpass US$ 25 billion by 2030.
The manufacturing chain spans complex small-molecule 
synthesis for cytotoxic payloads, purpose-designed linker 
chemistry, high-containment process development, conventional 
and site-specific bioconjugation, purification, analytical 
characterisation, bioassays and translational pharmacology. Each 
step generates data that informs the next. Cohance’s ADC platform 
connects high-potency payload and linker-payload chemistry 
in India with NJ Bio’s bioconjugation, analytics, bioassays and 
translational-research capabilities in the United States.
Cohance has built an integrated ADC value chain that connects 
each of these capabilities under one platform. NJ Bio, the 
bioconjugation and translational research engine, operates a plate-
based workflow enabling parallel evaluation of antibody-payload 
combinations through conjugation, purification, binding assays 
and cytotoxicity screening. Its translational platform extends into 
pharmacology, PK/ADME, toxicology, immune profiling and in-vivo  
evaluation.
In FY26, NJ Bio completed five GMP bioconjugation batches, 
supported an end-to-end ADC drug-product programme through 
Phase I, and advanced customised payload programmes. One 
programme progressed to Phase III. One new ADC-payload drug 
master file was submitted. Three additional filings were in progress. 
The planned US cGMP expansion will support ADC supply through 
Phase 2b by FY2026–27.

THE OLIGONUCLEOTIDE  
FRONTIER
THE STORY
Most medicines work by acting on proteins — the molecules that carry out 
functions in the body. But what if you could intervene earlier, at the level 
of the genetic instructions that create those proteins in the first place? That is 
the promise of oligonucleotide therapies — a class of medicines designed to 
correct, silence or modify genetic messages before they become disease.
It is one of the fastest-growing frontiers of modern medicine. But the chemistry 
required to manufacture these therapies is among the most exacting in the 
pharmaceutical world — requiring specialised building blocks, precision 
assembly and purification processes that operate at the molecular scale. Few 
organisations in the world possess this capability. Fewer still can connect it to 
the broader drug development chain.
Cohance can. The same platform that builds the molecular components 
for oligonucleotide therapies also operates the conjugation technology 
to attach them to targeting agents — antibodies, ligands, delivery vehicles 
— creating the next generation of precision medicines. A pharmaceutical 
company developing one of these therapies does not need to assemble a 
coalition of specialists. It needs one partner.
Through Sapala, Cohance brings specialised capabilities in modified 
nucleosides, phosphoramidites, complex building blocks and emerging 
nucleic-acid chemistries. The connection with NJ Bio’s conjugation and 
translational capabilities also creates the potential to participate in next-
generation formats such as ligand-conjugated siRNAs and antibody-
oligonucleotide conjugates.
This combination extends Cohance’s relevance beyond individual building 
blocks towards broader nucleic acid and conjugation opportunities.
Cohance Lifesciences Limited
8
=== page 12 ===
Oligonucleotide-based therapies — antisense, siRNA, mRNA 
and their conjugated variants — target disease at the 
nucleic-acid level. Their manufacture demands specialised 
chemistry: nucleoside modification, phosphoramidite 
synthesis, solid-phase oligonucleotide assembly, purification 
at scale and analytical characterisation against stringent 
pharmacopoeial standards.
Sapala Organics, integrated within the Cohance platform, 
brings a deep legacy in nucleic-acid chemistry — from 
modified nucleosides and speciality phosphoramidites 
through to oligonucleotide synthesis and conjugation. This is a 
scientific foundation built over years of process development, 
analytical method refinement and regulatory-grade 
manufacturing.
The connection between Sapala’s nucleic-acid platform 
and NJ Bio’s conjugation and translational capabilities 
enables Cohance to support next-generation conjugate 
formats: antibody-oligonucleotide conjugates, ligand-
conjugated siRNAs and targeted RNA therapeutics. The same 
analytical infrastructure that characterises a payload-linker 
intermediate characterises an oligonucleotide conjugate. The 
same quality systems that govern GMP bioconjugation govern 
the oligonucleotide supply chain.THE SCIENCE

Dear Shareholders,
I write to you for the first time as Executive Chairman and Group CEO 
of Cohance Lifesciences. I accept this responsibility with humility, 
conviction and a clear sense of purpose.
Across more than three decades in global pharmaceuticals, one lesson 
has remained constant: enduring institutions are built where science, 
purpose, quality and disciplined execution come together. Cohance has 
that foundation. Suven Pharma, Avra, Sapala and NJ Bio each carry a 
distinctive scientific legacy, built through patient investment, exacting 
chemistry, trusted customer relationships and deeply experienced 
teams. Our opportunity is to connect these strengths into one science-
led platform that can support increasingly complex molecules from 
development to commercial supply.
Annual Report 2025-26Corporate Overview
13

=== page 17 ===
We enter this phase in a demanding environment and at a 
time of organisational transition. We approach it with candour 
and a long-term perspective. Our task is to preserve the 
scientific depth within each business, link it more deliberately 
and translate it into stronger outcomes for customers, patients, 
communities and shareholders.
Advancing Science Through One  
Connected Platform
The future of medicine is being shaped by greater molecular 
complexity. Antibody–drug conjugates, oligonucleotides, 
peptides, chiral intermediates and other complex small 
molecules require specialised chemistry, analytical depth, 
containment and reliable scale-up. Cohance is positioned 
across this life-sciences value chain—from route design and 
process development to clinical supply and commercial 
manufacturing.
Suven Pharma contributes an innovator-focused CDMO 
heritage in complex process chemistry and commercial 
manufacturing. Avra adds specialised chemistry and advanced 
intermediates. Sapala brings differentiated expertise in 
oligonucleotide building blocks and emerging nucleic-acid 
chemistries. NJ Bio extends the platform into payload-linker 
science, bioconjugation, analytics, bioassays and translational 
research. Together, these capabilities allow us to connect 
scientific decisions across the development pathway and 
support customers with greater continuity.
We are investing behind this direction. The cGMP expansion 
at NJ Bio is intended to extend support for ADC programmes 
through Phase 2b clinical supply. The oligonucleotide 
building-block facility at Nacharam is progressing towards 
commercial readiness. In small-molecule Pharma CDMO, at the 
beginning of FY26, we indicated that four customer molecules 
from our Phase III pipeline were expected to progress to 
commercial supply over an 18–24-month period. Two of 
these molecules have since entered commercial supply, with 
deliveries scheduled across Q2 and Q3 FY27. The remaining 
two are expected to enter commercial supply over the next 
12–15 months. One of these customer molecules has received 
US FDA approval, enabling the customer to progress towards 
commercial launch. This progress, together with our long-
standing relationships with the world’s leading pharmaceutical 
innovators, provides a strong foundation for deepening 
collaboration across the combined platform.
Life Sciences and Speciality Chemicals
Our role in the life-sciences value chain carries an important 
responsibility. The work performed in our laboratories and 
plants supports the development and dependable supply 
of medicines. Customers therefore look to us for chemistry, 
quality, regulatory discipline, speed, continuity and the ability 
to solve problems across a molecule’s lifecycle. By integrating discovery-enabling science, process development, scale-up 
and manufacturing, Cohance can help reduce hand-offs, 
improve learning and enable more reliable progress from an 
idea to a medicine.
Speciality Chemicals is a complementary expression of 
the same chemistry-led capability, organised around two 
verticals. In AgChem CDMO, we partner with innovators to 
develop, scale and commercially produce complex molecules 
for crop protection — work that contributes directly to 
agricultural productivity and food security at a time when 
a growing global population, shifting weather patterns and 
urbanisation-driven reductions in arable land make that 
mission more urgent than ever. In Performance Chemicals, we 
work with innovators to enhance the efficiency of products 
in display electronics and advanced coatings, helping reduce 
the carbon footprint of products and applications while 
supporting consumer wellbeing. Across both verticals, we are 
deepening engagement with innovators in the US, Japan and 
Europe, advancing new active-ingredient and registration-
related opportunities, and selectively building capabilities 
in next-generation electronic and performance materials. 
Our focus will remain on specialised, technically demanding 
opportunities where science and execution create durable 
value.
Quality and Safety: Non-negotiable Foundations
Scientific capability has value only when it is supported by 
uncompromising quality and safety. These are not compliance 
functions at the edge of our operations; they are fundamental 
to every decision, every batch and every promise we make. 
In the coming year, we will strengthen both through clear 
ownership, independent assurance and measurable execution.
Process safety is foundational to how we operate, and we are 
raising the bar. During the year, we initiated a comprehensive 
programme of HAZOP reviews, defined safeguards and 
independent third-party audits across our commercial-
reaction sites, with a clear roadmap to cover every facility in 
the network. In parallel, we are advancing hydrogenation 
safety through semi-automation, closed-system transfers 
and planned facility upgrades designed to reduce operator 
exposure at source. The objective is to embed strong process-
safety discipline into the way every project is designed, scaled 
and operated: as a design principle from the outset.
Quality at Cohance must be designed into our systems, 
visible in our data and consistent across the network. We 
are accelerating a digital compliance and data-integrity 
programme across our regulatory sites, progressing toward full 
electronic audit trails, comprehensive training coverage and 
structured cross-contamination risk assessments that underpin 
cleaning validation. These represent a shift toward a quality 
architecture that is audit-ready by design and scalable with our 
growth.

Planned capital expenditure will support ADC expansion,

deployed with discipline and linked to clear scientific, safety, 
quality and customer priorities. The opportunity before us is 
significant. The more enduring measure of our progress will 
be the strength of the institution, we build and the value we 
create for our customers.
A Year of Transition, Supported by Resilience
FY26 was a demanding year. Consolidated revenue stood at 
₹22.68 billion and adjusted EBITDA at ₹4.8 billion, representing 
a consolidated margin of 21%. At the same time, gross 
margin improved to 70.8%, up 209 basis points year on 
year, supported by product mix, backward integration and 
operating efficiencies. We closed the year with net cash of 
₹1.53 billion, providing a foundation from which to invest 
through cycles and build our newer platforms with patience.
The true measure of a science-led organisation is the relevance

aggregation for its own sake. It is to create one institution 
in which every scientific capability becomes more valuable 
through its connection with the others.With Gratitude

ABOUT  
THE REPORT
Reporting Framework
The Integrated Report of Cohance Lifesciences has been 
prepared in accordance with the principles of the International 
Framework issued by the IFRS Foundation, which promotes 
integrated thinking and focuses on how the organisation 
creates, preserves and sustains value over the short, medium 
and long term.
The report adopts a multi-capital approach, demonstrating 
how the Company utilises and transforms six capitals, namely, 
Financial, Manufactured, Intellectual, Human, Social & 
Relationship and Natural Capital, to create sustainable value. 
Reporting Boundary
This Integrated Report covers Cohance Lifesciences Limited and its subsidiaries and operations over which the Company 
exercises management control. FY26 represents the first reporting period following the merger and integration of multiple 
entities into Cohance Lifesciences. Unless otherwise stated, all financial and non-financial information presented in this report 
pertains to the consolidated reporting boundary.The report is further aligned with the Securities and Exchange 
Board of India’s Business Responsibility and Sustainability 
Reporting (BRSR) framework and the United Nations 
Sustainable Development Goals (UN SDGs) to articulate the 
Company’s broader economic, environmental and social 
contributions.
Through this integrated approach, Cohance presents a 
holistic view of its strategy, governance, risks, performance 
and future outlook as it advances its ambition of becoming a 
differentiated, technology-led global CRDMO platform.

Reporting Period
This Integrated Report covers the financial year from April 
1, 2025 to March 31, 2026 (FY26). Cohance Lifesciences 
publishes this Integrated Report on an annual basis. The 
financial and non-financial information presented herein 
pertains to this reporting period unless otherwise stated. To 
enhance comparability and reflect the expanded reporting 
boundary following the merger and integration of multiple

necessary and practicable, in accordance with applicable 
accounting and reporting requirements.
Materiality
Cohance Lifesciences follows a structured materiality 
assessment process to identify and prioritise the issues that 
have the greatest influence on long-term value creation and 
stakeholder decision-making. The assessment considers inputs 
from internal and external stakeholders, including the Board 
of Directors, executive leadership, employees, customers, 
investors, regulatory authorities and industry experts. 
Material topics are evaluated based on their significance to 
stakeholders and their potential impact on the Company’s 
strategy, operations, financial performance and sustainability 
outcomes.
The results of the assessment directly inform the content and 
priorities of this Integrated Report. Topics identified as material 
receive enhanced disclosure and performance reporting, while 
matters considered less material are addressed in proportion 
to their significance and impact on the business.
Data and Assurance
Financial information presented in this Integrated Report has 
been prepared in accordance with the applicable provisions 
of the Companies Act, 2013 and Indian Accounting Standards 
(Ind AS) and has been audited by the Company’s statutory 
auditors. Non-financial and sustainability information has 
been compiled through internal data collection and validation 
processes and is subject to management review.
Selected non-financial disclosures contained in this Integrated 
Report have been independently assured by Sustainability 
Actions Private Limited. The assurance has been conducted 
in accordance with BRSR Core assessment standards and 
covers all BRSR data points on a standalone basis. The level 
of assurance provided is Reasonable. Further details of the 
assurance approach, scope, methodology, exclusions and 
assurance statement are presented in the BRSR section of  
this report.Comparability and Restatements
FY25 and FY26 figures are not directly comparable due to 
the merger and integration of multiple entities into Cohance 
Lifesciences during FY26 and the consequent expansion of 
the reporting boundary. To enhance comparability, certain

or restated, wherever considered necessary and practicable, 
in accordance with applicable accounting and reporting 
requirements. These restatements primarily affect year-on-year 
comparability of certain financial and non-financial metrics 
due to the expanded consolidated reporting boundary.

COMPANY  OVERVIEW
SCIENCE, SCALE AND 
INNOVATION.GLOBALLY INTEGRATED CDMO  
ENABLING COMPLEX THERAPEUTICS THROUGH
Positioned at the intersection of innovation, integration and growth
Cohance Lifesciences is a science-led contract development 
and manufacturing organisation serving global 
pharmaceutical innovators, biotechnology companies and 
generic pharmaceutical customers. Its operations span 
Pharma CDMO, API+ and Speciality Chemicals, supported by 
specialised capabilities in small molecules, antibody-drug 
conjugates and oligonucleotides.
The platform combines research, process development, 
analytical capabilities, high-containment chemistry and 
commercial-scale manufacturing across India and the 
United States. This enables Cohance to support customer 
programmes across development, scale-up, clinical supply and 
commercial manufacturing.
The Company’s operating model is built around three 
priorities: scientific differentiation, reliable execution and long-
term customer partnerships.
Cohance’s business ecosystem comprises global 
pharmaceutical innovators, biotechnology companies, 
suppliers of specialised raw materials and intermediates, 
contract partners, technology collaborators, regulators and 
research institutions, with whom the Company maintains long-
term strategic relationships across its value chain. All of its product and service categories are subject to 
rigorous quality, safety and regulatory assessment processes 
throughout development and commercialisation to ensure 
compliance with applicable pharmaceutical standards and 
customer requirements. Product and service information, 
labelling and documentation are prepared in accordance with 
applicable pharmaceutical regulations, customer specifications 
and market-specific regulatory requirements.
Cohance Lifesciences Limited is a publicly held company 
incorporated in India as a Public Limited Company under the 
provisions of the Companies Act, 2013, with its equity shares 
listed on the National Stock Exchange of India Limited (NSE) 
and BSE Limited. Headquartered in Hyderabad, Telangana, 
India, the Company operates manufacturing, research and

SUSTAINABILITY GOVERNANCE AND COMMITMENTS
Cohance aligns its sustainability framework with globally recognised standards through annual CEO commitments to the United 
Nations Global Compact (UNGC) and its universal sustainability principles. The Company’s approach integrates environmental 
stewardship, responsible operations, workforce well-being and governance integrity into long-term strategic decision-making.
ESG METRICS AND PERFORMANCE TRACKING
   
  Environmental Stewardship
Cohance has established a rigorous, time-bound 
decarbonisation agenda underpinned by science-aligned 
targets. The Company is committed to reducing absolute SBTi 
Services has validated that the greenhouse gas emissions 
reduction target(s) submitted by Cohance Lifesciences Limited 
which conform with the SBTi Criteria and Recommendations 
(Near-Term Criteria V5.3 And Net-Zero Criteria V1.3).
Complementing this climate ambition, Cohance is pursuing 
a near-one-third reduction in specific water consumption, a 
measurable drawdown in hazardous waste sent to landfill and 
a progressive transition toward renewable energy across its 
global operations.
The Company’s environmental credentials have earned 
independent validation: CDP has assigned a ‘B’ rating for 
Climate Change and an ‘A−’ rating for Water Security — 
external affirmations of the robustness and credibility of its 
sustainability programme.
 
  Social Capital & Human Performance
Cohance recognises that long-term value creation is 
inseparable from the strength and well-being of its people. 
The Company is actively advancing gender diversity across 
all levels of the workforce, with defined targets to elevate women’s representation over the medium term. Alongside this, 
Cohance is committed to meaningfully reducing attrition —  
a strategic priority that reflects its focus on talent retention, 
organisational continuity and employee experience.
On occupational health and safety, the Company upholds 
universal participation in training programmes across its 
workforce and reported zero reportable lost-time injuries 
during the period under review. This milestone speaks to the 
depth of its safety culture and operational discipline.
 
  Governance & Ethical Integrity
Cohance holds its governance framework to an 
uncompromising standard. The Company targets zero ethical 
or regulatory non-compliances, embedding accountability 
at every level of the organisation. This is reinforced through 
mandatory acknowledgement of the Code of Conduct by 
all employees and Board members — a firm commitment to 
transparency, integrity and the highest standards of corporate 
behaviour.
Collectively, these governance disciplines ensure that 
Cohance’s ESG commitments are not aspirational declarations, 
but institutionalised obligations with clear lines of 
accountability.
INTEGRATION INTO CAPITAL ALLOCATION, R&D AND 
SUPPLY CHAIN PRACTICES
Capital Allocation & Operational Efficiency
Sustainability is not a parallel agenda at Cohance — it is embedded directly into how capital is deployed.
Third-party renewable power purchase agreements are now active across key facilities, marking a tangible step in the 
Company’s decarbonisation journey. In parallel, engineering and R&D teams are driving measurable efficiency gains through 
catalyst recovery, solvent recycling and focused value-engineering programmes. The objective is clear: leaner processes, lower 
environmental impact, stronger returns.

=== page 33 ===
1.
Reclaimed Products and Packaging Materials
Owing to the highly regulated nature of pharmaceutical manufacturing and the Company’s business model as an integrated 
CRDMO, Cohance Lifesciences does not currently operate product or packaging take-back programmes or reclaim products and 
packaging materials after customer use. Consequently, reclaimed products and packaging materials do not constitute a material 
aspect of the Company’s operations and no quantities were reported for FY26.
Responsible supply chain management
Cohance holds its supply chain to the same standards it sets for its own operations. The Company is progressing toward full 
Pharmaceutical Supply Chain Initiative (PSCI) Supplier Partner status — a recognised benchmark for responsible procurement 
in the industry. This commitment has been independently validated by strong performance in the Together for Sustainability 
(TfS) audit framework, demonstrating that Cohance’s supply chain practices meet rigorous global standards. Transparency, 
accountability and sustainability are no longer aspirations in procurement. At Cohance, there are requirements.
 
01  
Environmental Due Diligence in Supplier 
Onboarding
As part of its responsible sourcing framework, Cohance 
integrates environmental considerations into supplier 
onboarding. During FY26, nearly 300+ new suppliers were 
onboarded, of which 100% underwent environmental 
screening prior to engagement. The assessment considered 
environmental regulatory compliance, environmental 
management systems (including ISO 14001 certification, 
where applicable), waste management practices, greenhouse 
gas management, water stewardship, hazardous material 
handling and alignment with the Together for Sustainability 
(TfS) and Pharmaceutical Supply Chain Initiative (PSCI) 
principles.
 
02 
Management of Environmental Impacts in the 
Supply Chain
Cohance periodically evaluates the environmental 
performance of its suppliers through supplier assessments, 
Together for Sustainability (TfS) audits and due diligence 
reviews. During FY26, 62% of value chain partners (by 
value of business conducted) were assessed. No suppliers 
were identified as having actual or potential significant 
environmental impacts, and accordingly, no corrective action 
plans, remediation measures or follow-up assessments were 
required. Further, no supplier relationships were discontinued 
during the year on account of environmental non-compliance. 
 03 
Social Criteria in Supplier Selection and Onboarding
Cohance is committed to partnering with suppliers 
that uphold high standards of ethics, human rights and 
responsible workforce practices. During FY26, 100% of all 
newly onboarded suppliers were screened against defined 
social criteria prior to engagement. The assessment covered 
key aspects including labour practices, occupational health 
and safety, human rights, prevention of child and forced 
labour, employee welfare, ethical business conduct, and 
alignment with the Pharmaceutical Supply Chain Initiative 
(PSCI) principles. This screening process helps ensure that 
new supplier relationships are built on a strong foundation of 
responsible and sustainable business practices. 
 
04 
Management of Social Impacts in the Supply Chain
Cohance periodically monitors the social performance of 
its suppliers through structured assessments, sustainability 
evaluations and due diligence processes. During FY26, 62% 
of value chain partners (by value of business conducted) 
were assessed for compliance with the Company’s social 
performance expectations. The assessments did not identify 
any actual or potential significant social impacts, and therefore 
no remediation or corrective actions were required. No 
supplier relationships were terminated during the year due to 
social non-compliance or unresolved social concerns.

CAPEX 
Cohance deployed ₹215 Crore in capital expenditure 
during FY26. A significant share was directed towards 
differentiated, high-growth platforms. Key investments 
included the expansion of the bioconjugation cGMP suite at 
NJ Bio in Princeton; a cGMP oligonucleotide building-block 
facility at Nacharam, Hyderabad; and high-containment 
capability upgrades at the same site. Capacity expansion and infrastructure enhancement across Suryapet, Parawada and 
Vizag, alongside quality and compliance upgrades, completed 
the programme.
Looking ahead, capex is expected to sustain investment 
momentum across differentiated technology platforms and 
the integrated manufacturing network.
GREENFIELD/BROWNFIELD EXPANSION
Cohance’s capital expenditure programme is centred on brownfield expansion — building new capabilities and suites within 
existing facilities to accelerate delivery and optimise capital efficiency.
NJ BIO, PRINCETON (US) 
A US$10 million investment is underway to construct a 
dedicated cGMP bioconjugation suite, scaling ADC supply 
capacity through Phase 2b clinical requirements. For future 
commercial needs, a semi-built facility within the adjacent 
pharma park provides rapid-conversion infrastructure as 
customer molecules advance.NACHARAM, HYDERABAD 
A ₹23 Crore investment is creating a multi-kilo cGMP 
oligonucleotide building block facility with a capacity of up 
to 700 kg/year, Under Validation stage. A dedicated high-
containment block capable of handling compounds up to 
OEB6  have commissioned to support customised Payload-
linker programmes for innovators.
VIZAG ANDHRA PRADESH 
The dedicated Vizag site has earmarked space for future 
capacity expansion, providing a structured runway for growth 
as demand scales.OTHER SITES 
Brownfield capacity augmentation at Suryapet and high-

complete the current programme.

REGULATORY AUDITS AND RE-QUALIFICATION 
Cohance’s compliance track record across global regulatory frameworks reflects its commitment to quality, patient safety and 
regulatory excellence — reinforcing stakeholder trust and long-term investment proposition. FY26 saw significant regulatory 
activity across the manufacturing network.
NACHARAM FORMULATIONS SITE
The facility received an OAI classification from the US FDA, 
followed by a Warning Letter in February 2026. The Company 
initiated a voluntary, temporary shutdown to implement 
comprehensive remediation, CAPAs and quality system 
upgrades with external expert support. Production and 
shipments have since resumed in a phased manner for non-US 
markets; resumption of US supply will progress as utilisation 
normalises.
JAGGAIAHPET API SITE
The facility — a significant revenue contributor — cleared its 
US FDA audit with zero observations.VIZAG FACILITY
Successfully completed a critical business continuity audit 
conducted by a large Japanese innovator customer.
PLATFORM-WIDE
During FY26, Cohance’s facilities underwent 12 regulatory 
audits and hosted 143 customer audits, along with 36 
customer visits. Eleven regulatory audits were successfully 
closed, with CAPA implementation progressing for the 
remaining audit. This reflects the strength of Cohance’s quality 
systems and continued customer engagement across its 
manufacturing platform.

MERGER INTEGRATION AND ORGANISATIONAL CULTURE
Post-merger, Cohance focused on three priorities: leadership stability, operational integration and cultural alignment. The 
Company transitioned to a three-SBU structure — Pharma CDMO, API+ and Speciality Chemicals — with dedicated CXO 
appointments to sharpen accountability and drive execution. A structured organisational upgrade programme is embedding 
a performance-driven, customer-first, science-led culture across all business units. This transformation is not cosmetic — it is 
architectural, designed to position Cohance as a unified, high-performance CRDMO platform built for scale.
ANNUAL COMPENSATION RATIO
As part of its commitment to transparency in remuneration practices, the Company discloses employee compensation metrics. 
During FY26, the median annual compensation of all employees was ₹6,56,688 excluding the highest paid individual. The ratio 
of the annual total compensation of the highest-paid individual to the median annual compensation of all employees (excluding 
the highest-paid individual) was 287:1. The highest-paid individual received no increase in annual total compensation during the 
year, compared with a median increase of 11% for all employees.
ENTRY-LEVEL COMPENSATION AND FAIR WAGE PRACTICES 
Cohance Lifesciences is committed to fair and equitable remuneration practices. The Company ensures that entry-level 
wages across its operations meet or exceed applicable statutory minimum wage requirements and are determined without 
discrimination based on gender. Standard entry-level compensation is periodically reviewed with reference to local market 
conditions, regulatory requirements and internal compensation principles.

=== page 62 ===
RESEARCH & DEVELOPMENT FRAMEWORK
Cohance’s R&D framework is built on three pillars: specialist talent, niche technology platforms and an 
integrated global infrastructure. Together, they underpin the Company’s evolution into a leading strategic 
CRDMO partner.
Dedicated Talent Pool and Leadership Focus
640 scientists form the backbone of Cohance’s R&D engine. 
A structured organisational upgrade programme has 
deepened technical and leadership capability — with targeted 
investments across R&D, Quality and Regulatory functions at 
the senior executive level. Guiding this effort is the External 
Advisory Board (EAB) — five global pharma innovators who 
actively steer R&D investments toward advanced payload 
diversification, oligonucleotide scale-up and complex small-
molecule platforms.
Specialised Niche Technology Platforms
Cohance’s process R&D is oriented around continuous 
improvement, process intensification and execution speed 
across complex chemistries. Four core modalities define the 
platform:Antibody-Drug Conjugates (ADCs): Focus areas 
include expanding the payload-linker library, advancing 
Topoisomerase-I payload architectures, developing 
customised exatecan-linked assets and progressing DMF 
submissions. Clinical collaborations are actively broadening 
the pipeline.
Oligonucleotides and mRNA: Cohance masters 
conformationally constrained nucleic acid chemistry — 
supplying high-purity Tricyclo-DNA amidites and developing 
complex building blocks for oligonucleotides, siRNA and 
Antibody-Oligonucleotide Conjugates (AOCs).
High-Purity Speciality Chemistry: R&D supports lab-scale 
programmes, registration samples and validation campaigns 
for advanced intermediates in agrochemicals and high-purity 
electronic materials, including OLED intermediates.
Small Molecules: The platform is anchored in hazardous 
chemistry scale-up, complex chiral synthesis and multi-step 
synthesis. Capabilities in Flow Chemistry and Peptides are 
being expanded — both organically and inorganically.
Integrated India-US Infrastructure
Cohance operates a seamless end-to-end global model — 
separating early-stage problem-solving from commercial 
scale-up:
NJ Bio (USA): It serves as the early-stage scientific arm. 
Working with over 100 innovator and biotech accounts, it 
handles discovery, payload-linker synthesis, analytical method 
development and bioconjugation support through Phase II.
India Innovation Centres: They take programmes forward 
once the IND filing is achieved. Complex multi-step synthesis 
and commercial-scale payload-linker production are executed 
within highly specialised infrastructure — including high-
containment blocks engineered to OEB4 and OEB6 standards 
for potent cytotoxic chemistry.
Sapala Organics (India): It complements the network with 
specialised nucleic acid chemistry and complex oligomer 
building blocks — systematically building toward full cGMP 
manufacturing capability.
This operating model allows specialised scientific work to be 
allocated to the most appropriate teams and facilities while 
maintaining coordinated programme oversight.
Annual Report 2025-26Corporate Overview

=== page 63 ===
PROPRIETARY PROCESSES, PLATFORMS AND CORE IP
Cohance’s proprietary know-how is concentrated across 
technology platforms where process understanding, analytical 
control and specialised infrastructure create meaningful 
barriers to entry.
ADC & Bioconjugation (via NJ Bio): NJ Bio is the heart of 
Cohance’s ADC intellectual property. Its proprietary know-how 
spans payload customisation, linker design, payload-linker 
synthesis and bioconjugation processes — built through years 
of hands-on clinical collaboration.
Cohance’s Intellectual repository: The Company has a 
library of over 500 payload-linkers and a globally recognised 
leadership position in Topoisomerase-I payloads — covering 
S-Trione, SN-38, Exatecan and DXd. Few CDMOs globally can 
match this repository. The platform is also expanding into 
next-generation modalities: PEGylated antibody conjugates, 
siRNA conjugates and Antibody-Oligonucleotide Conjugates 
(AOCs) — positioning Cohance at the cutting edge of 
bioconjugation science.Oligonucleotides: Cohance has established differentiated 
capabilities in oligonucleotide and nucleic-acid chemistry 
through its subsidiary. Sapala brings deep expertise in 
advanced oligonucleotide technologies, complex amidite and 
nucleoside building blocks, specialised phosphoramidites and 
GalNAc chemistry. The Company also participates in the supply 
chain for tricyclo-DNA (tc-DNA) amidites for a global innovator, 
demonstrating its ability to execute complex synthesis and 
manufacture critical building blocks requiring significant 
scientific and process capabilities.
Small Molecules: Cohance’s small molecule platform is built 
for complexity. Core capabilities include hazardous chemistry 
scale-up, complex chiral synthesis, multi-step synthesis 
and high-containment infrastructure engineered to OEB6 
standards. Flow Chemistry and Peptide capabilities are actively 
under development — extending the platform’s reach into the 
next generation of high-value synthetic modalities.

NEW PRODUCT INTRODUCTION RATE/MOLECULES IN DEVELOPMENT
Pharma CDMO: The Pharma CDMO pipeline is deep and 
advancing. Over 140+ active projects span Phase 1 through

market recognition and the compelling pull of Cohance’s 
differentiated capabilities.API+: Cohance accelerated its API+ pipeline with intent. FY26

Scalable Processes
Technology in Action l Continuous Flow Chemistry
BRINGING CONTROL TO A HIGHLY EXOTHERMIC REACTION
A continuous-flow approach transformed a difficult reaction into a safer and scalable process.
ADVANCING THE SCIENCE OF PROGRESS
TURNING COMPLEX CHEMISTRY
INTO BETTER PROCESSES
Three examples illustrate how our flow-chemistry and biocatalysis platforms can improve process safety, product quality and 
manufacturing efficiency. Our technology platforms allow us to look beyond whether a reaction can be achieved and focus on 
how it can be improved. By combining deep chemistry experience with advanced development capabilities, our scientists are 
creating processes with better control, higher product quality and greater manufacturing efficiency.
The following examples demonstrate the scientific, operational and commercial relevance of our capabilities.
Safer Chemistry
 Cleaner Outcomes
 
01
 The challenge
The reaction released significant heat when conducted in 
a conventional batch process. Managing this exothermicity 
safely, while maintaining consistent quality, was critical 
before the process could be considered for larger-scale 
manufacturing.
  Our approach
Our scientists redesigned the process using plug-flow reactors. 
The reaction was carried out continuously in a controlled 
stream, allowing heat generation and reaction conditions to 
be managed more precisely.  The outcome
The redesigned process delivered the product at 82% yield 
and more than 99% purity. A 50 g sample was generated, 
followed by three 100 g laboratory batches that demonstrated 
consistent product quality. The process was established 
as scalable and economically viable for commercial 
manufacturing.
82% yield  l  >99% purity  l  Consistent quality across multiple batches
This case demonstrates how flow chemistry can improve process safety and control while creating a practical route from 
laboratory development to commercial manufacturing.

Technology in Action l Photo-Flow Chemistry
USING LIGHT AND FLOW TO IMPROVE PRODUCT QUALITY
A light-assisted continuous process improved yield while eliminating a key impurity.
Technology in Action l Biocatalysis
HARNESSING ENZYMES FOR HIGH SELECTIVITY
An enzyme-led process achieved high purity and yield under mild operating conditions.
 02
 
03 The challenge
A bromination reaction conducted through the conventional 
process generated an unwanted di-bromo impurity. Reducing 
this impurity, while improving the reaction yield, was 
important to strengthen the overall process.
  Our approach
The team developed a photo-flow process in which the 
reaction was conducted continuously under controlled light. 
This provided more precise control over the reaction and 
helped limit the formation of the unwanted by-product.
 The challenge
Producing the required chiral form of a molecule can require 
complex reaction conditions and multiple purification steps. 
The objective was to develop a more selective process that 
could deliver the desired form efficiently.
  Our approach
Our scientists developed a ketoreductase-based process. The 
enzyme was used to guide the reaction selectively at room 
temperature, and the process was subsequently demonstrated 
at kilogram scale.  The outcome
The photo-flow approach increased the product yield and 
reduced the di-bromo impurity from 1% to non-detectable 
levels. The cleaner reaction profile can also reduce the burden 
on subsequent purification steps.
  The outcome
The process achieved more than 99.8% chiral purity and a yield 
of over 93%. Its successful demonstration at kilogram scale 
provides a foundation for further scale-up.Higher yield  l  Di-bromo impurity reduced from 1% to non-detectable
The work illustrates how combining light-based chemistry with continuous processing can deliver cleaner products and 
more efficient manufacturing routes.
>99.8% chiral purity  l  >93% yield  l  Demonstrated at kilogram scale
This case highlights how biocatalysis can combine high selectivity with gentler operating conditions, supporting more 
efficient and sustainable process development.

Top 10 customers and nature of contractual 
relationships 
Cohance works with the top 20 global innovators. These 
relationships account for over 85% of revenues in the Small 
Molecules segment. They are deeply integrated, structured 
as long-term commercial supply agreements governed by 
formal Confidentiality Agreements (CDAs) and Master Service 
Agreements (MSAs). These are multi-year manufacturing 
mandates and Lifecycle management partnerships. The 
opposite of transactional.
Average contract duration 
Contracts across the CDMO and API segments are multi-
year, with specific supply obligations built in. Some include 
minimum purchase orders, depending on the predictability of 
the drug’s commercial launch.
Exclusivity arrangements 
Cohance holds exclusivity in areas where few others can 
operate. The Company is the exclusive payload-intermediate 
supplier to a major innovator in its ADC pipeline. It is also the We also participates in the supply chain for tricyclo-DNA 
(tc-DNA) amidites for a global innovator.  These positions are 
earned through capability, sustained through consistency.

Western CDMOs: Cohance partners with Western CDMOs to

commercial Key Starting Material (KSM) contract already in 
execution.
Agrochemical and Speciality Innovators: The Company

and European agrochemical companies. It also maintains 
partnerships in niche electronic chemicals, including OLED 
materials.
External Advisory Board (EAB): Five respected industry

Company’s scientific and technological roadmap.

Cohance recognises that its manufacturing intensity places a direct demand on natural

intent to improve year on year. The goal is to operate at scale without compromising the ecosystems and

=== page 87 ===
Climate action and decarbonisation 
Cohance operates 13 manufacturing plants. Each facility 
consumes energy, water and raw materials on an industrial 
scale. Climate change is material to the Company due to its 
implications for operational resilience, energy costs, regulatory 
requirements, customer expectations and long-term value 
creation. The Company manages climate-related impacts 
through decarbonisation initiatives, renewable energy 
adoption, resource efficiency programmes and periodic 
performance reviews overseen by management and the Board.
Climate Transition Roadmap: Cohance Lifesciences’ Carbon 
Transition Plan is centred on accelerating the transition to 
a lower-carbon business model through renewable energy 
adoption, operational efficiency improvements and value 
chain decarbonisation. The roadmap integrates energy 
transition initiatives, resource-efficient manufacturing 
practices, low-carbon technologies, circular resource 
management and responsible procurement principles to 
progressively reduce the Company’s greenhouse gas footprint. 
Through a combination of decarbonisation initiatives across 
its operations and supply chain, Cohance seeks to strengthen 
climate resilience, enhance resource efficiency and advance its 
long-term net-zero ambition.Climate Resilience and Adaptation: The Company 
periodically assesses physical climate risks including water 
stress, extreme weather events, supply chain disruptions 
and energy availability. Adaptation measures include water 
recycling infrastructure, business continuity planning, resilient 
utilities and diversification of sourcing arrangements.
The Company’s transition to a lower-carbon economy seeks to 
create long-term opportunities in renewable energy, resource 
efficiency and sustainable manufacturing while supporting 
employee capability building and minimising adverse social 
impacts associated with operational changes.
Climate change presents both risks and opportunities that 
may influence operational resilience, cost structures, supply 
chain continuity and long-term growth prospects. Cohance 
periodically evaluates climate-related risks and opportunities 
and integrates appropriate mitigation and adaptation 
measures into its strategic and operational planning.

Biodiversity and ecosystem stewardship
Biodiversity Policy and Commitments
Cohance Lifesciences maintains a dedicated Biodiversity 
Policy focused on habitat protection, ecological responsibility 
and compliance with environmental laws and regulations. 
Preserving and enhancing biodiversity forms an integral part 
of the Company’s sustainability strategy and its commitment 
to minimising environmental impacts on natural ecosystems. 
Biodiversity Risk Management
Biodiversity initiatives are implemented in consultation 
with relevant ecological experts, local authorities and other 
stakeholders, where appropriate. The Company strategically 
locates its operations to avoid environmentally sensitive 
areas, including biodiversity hotspots, UNESCO World 
Heritage Sites, Ramsar Wetlands and habitats associated with 
IUCN Red List species. Where operations are located near 
ecologically sensitive areas, Cohance applies a mitigation 
hierarchy based on avoidance, minimisation, restoration 
and offsetting. Biodiversity considerations are incorporated 
into Environmental Impact Assessments, biodiversity risk 
assessments and responsible sourcing practices.
Green Cover and Conservation Initiatives
Cohance maintains a minimum green cover of 33% across its 
manufacturing facilities and undertakes plantation initiatives 
within and around its operational locations. During FY25, the Company planted approximately 2,411 trees and initiated 
an additional programme to plant around 1,000 more trees. 
Beyond its operational boundaries, the Company has planted 
more than 100,000 native trees in Uttar Pradesh to create 
green corridors that improve habitat connectivity, facilitate 
safe elephant movement and support wildlife conservation. 
These initiatives are expected to enhance habitat connectivity, 
strengthen local ecosystem resilience and improve biodiversity 
outcomes over the long term.
Monitoring and Reporting
The Company monitors and reports biodiversity performance 
through its ESG framework and conducts periodic 
environmental assessments and site-level reviews to identify 
biodiversity-related risks and opportunities. Biodiversity 
performance is reported in alignment with applicable 
sustainability reporting frameworks, to strengthen biodiversity 
resilience and support long-term environmental sustainability. 
As of March 31, 2026, none of the Company’s manufacturing 
facilities are located within legally protected areas or 
designated Key Biodiversity Areas, except where specifically 
disclosed. Biodiversity considerations are integrated into 
environmental management processes to support informed 
decision-making and continuous improvement.

Water stewardship
Water is central to chemical synthesis. Cohance operates 
seven synthesis facilities, each with process interventions 
and water-recycling architectures designed to minimise fresh 
water dependency. Third-party freshwater consumption has 
decreased by 27% compared to the baseline.
The strategy is built on Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) assets and 
multi-stage recycling loops, particularly at the high-capacity 
manufacturing plants at Vizag and Nacharam. Every litre 
recovered is a litre that does not need to be sourced.
Management of water discharge-related impacts
Cohance manages water discharge impacts through an 
integrated framework comprising effluent segregation, 
treatment, recycling and continuous monitoring systems 
across its manufacturing facilities. Effluents generated from 
operations are treated through dedicated effluent treatment 
infrastructure and, at major manufacturing sites, are further 
processed through Zero Liquid Discharge (ZLD) systems 
that maximise water recovery and minimise releases to the 
environment. The Company monitors discharge quality 
parameters in accordance with applicable regulatory 
requirements and periodically reviews treatment system 
performance to prevent adverse impacts on receiving water 
bodies, ecosystems and neighbouring communities. Process 
optimisation, reuse initiatives and preventive controls are 
continuously strengthened to reduce pollutant loads and 
improve overall water stewardship performance.The formal target: reduce, reuse and recycle specific water 
consumption by 30% by 2030. Cohance benchmarks its 
water-related risks through the Carbon Disclosure Project 
(CDP) framework. The Company achieved an A- rating in Water 
Security in both 2024 and 2025.
Water as a shared resource
Water availability and quality are important considerations 
across Cohance’s manufacturing operations, given the water-
intensive nature of chemical synthesis processes. The Company 
recognises that freshwater resources are shared among 
industrial users, communities and ecosystems and therefore 
adopts a risk-based approach to water stewardship. Site-level 
assessments of water availability, operational dependency 
and potential impacts on surrounding communities and 
ecosystems are periodically undertaken through internal 
reviews and external frameworks such as CDP Water Security. 
Insights from these assessments inform conservation 
initiatives, water recycling investments and measures aimed at 
reducing freshwater dependency and strengthening long-
term water resilience across operations.
Water discharge volumes include treated effluents released 
from manufacturing and utility operations after applicable 
treatment processes. Water reused and recycled internally 
represents treated water recirculated within operations, 
including water recovered through Zero Liquid Discharge 
and multi-stage recycling systems at the Vizag and Nacharam 
facilities.

processing, recycling and coprocessing programmes designed 
to divert waste from landfill entirely.
Cohance applies the waste hierarchy of prevention, reduction, 
reuse, recycling and responsible disposal. Hazardous waste 
is segregated, stored and disposed of through authorised 
recyclers and treatment facilities. Waste performance is 
periodically monitored by the EHS function and reviewed by 
management.

an operational practice. Value engineering initiatives across the

recovered supports both environmental performance and 
financial margins.Waste generation and significant waste-related 
impacts

waste streams include spent solvents, catalyst residues, 
process sludge, packaging materials and general operational 
waste. If not responsibly managed, these waste streams 
can result in resource inefficiencies, increased disposal 
requirements and potential impacts on the environment. 
Accordingly, the Company focuses on waste minimisation, 
resource recovery and responsible disposal practices as 
integral components of its environmental stewardship and 
operational resilience strategy.

Why Materiality Matters
At Cohance Lifesciences, materiality serves as a critical 
link between stakeholder expectations, strategic priorities 
and long-term value creation. As a globally integrated 
CRDMO operating across complex and highly regulated 
pharmaceutical markets, the Company continuously evaluates 
the issues that have the greatest potential to influence 
business performance, stakeholder confidence and sustainable 
growth.
The materiality assessment enables Cohance to prioritise 
resources, strengthen risk management, guide capital 
allocation and focus on areas that are most relevant to its long-
term vision. By identifying and addressing these priorities, 
the Company seeks to create enduring value for stakeholders 
while advancing its ambition of becoming a leading global 
partner for complex pharmaceutical development and 
manufacturing.
Materiality Assessment Methodology
Cohance Lifesciences undertakes a structured and periodic 
materiality assessment process to identify, evaluate and 
prioritise the environmental, social, governance and business 
issues most relevant to its operations and long-term growth 
strategy.The assessment incorporates insights from stakeholder 
engagement activities, industry trends, regulatory 
developments, customer expectations, sustainability 
frameworks, emerging market opportunities and internal 
strategic priorities. The assessment considers actual and 
potential economic, environmental and social impacts arising 
from the Company’s operations and business relationships, 
including both positive and adverse impacts. Material topics 
are evaluated based on their significance to stakeholders 
and their potential impact on the Company’s ability to create 
value and achieve its strategic objectives. The assessment also 
considers actual and potential economic, environmental and 
social impacts arising from the Company’s operations and 
business relationships, including both positive and adverse 
impacts.
The identified topics are reviewed by senior management 
and aligned with the Company’s business strategy, risk 
management framework and sustainability commitments. This 
process ensures that material issues remain integrated into 
decision-making across operations, investments, capability 
development and stakeholder value creation initiatives and 
directly inform the content and priorities of this Integrated 
Report.

ENTERPRISE RISK MANAGEMENT
A PROACTIVE APPROACH     
FOR NAVIGATING UNCERTAINTY
At Cohance, risk management is not a compliance function. It is a strategic 
discipline. As the Company scales into advanced therapeutic modalities, 
new geographies and deeper customer partnerships, the ability to 
identify, assess and mitigate risk across every dimension of the business 
becomes a source of competitive advantage. Enterprise risk management 
is embedded within the strategic decision-making framework, ensuring 
that growth is pursued with discipline, not just ambition.
Cohance Lifesciences Limited
102
=== page 106 ===
Risk Management Philosophy
Cohance operates in markets where the consequences of failure are measured in patient safety, regulatory standing and 
institutional trust. The Company’s risk philosophy reflects this reality. Risk is not something to be eliminated. It is something to 
be understood, quantified and managed in proportion to the opportunity it accompanies. Every growth decision, every capital 
commitment, every new customer engagement carries risk. The Company’s obligation is to ensure that each risk is visible to 
leadership, assessed against clear criteria and addressed before it compounds. Cohance does not avoid complexity. It prepares 
for it.
Risk Management Framework
The enterprise risk management framework operates across four layers.
The outcome is an organisation that grows with awareness. Risks are surfaced early, addressed decisively and tracked until they 
are resolved. This is how Cohance protects stakeholder value while pursuing its long-term growth ambitions with confidence.

l Utilised dedicated high-containment manufacturing infrastructure and strengthened vertical integration to limit 
external exposure of critical processes and safeguard sensitive programmes.
l Reinforced governance and compliance frameworks for information security and data integrity.
Mitigation Measures
l Maintained a strong net cash-positive balance sheet and healthy liquidity profile, generating robust free cash flows 
despite a challenging operating environment.
l Improved working capital efficiency through tighter receivables and inventory management.
l Prioritised capital deployment toward differentiated platforms such as ADCs and oligonucleotides, with focused 
investments in manufacturing infrastructure and quality systems.
Mitigation Measures
l Established a dedicated three-SBU operating structure with clear leadership accountability, strengthening integration 
across commercial, scientific and operational functions.
l Leveraged cross-border capabilities to create an integrated end-to-end CRDMO platform, continuing to scale acquired 
capabilities through targeted investments and capability enhancement.
l Activated an External Advisory Board to guide integration, technology roadmaps and strategic execution.
Mitigation Measures
l Progressed toward a net-zero emissions pathway with SBTi-aligned targets, advancing renewable energy adoption 
across manufacturing facilities.
l Implemented water conservation, recycling and Zero Liquid Discharge initiatives alongside hazardous waste reduction 
and resource efficiency programmes.
l Strengthened sustainability disclosures and external ESG benchmarking through recognised frameworks.

THE FOUNDATION

At Cohance Lifesciences, strong governance forms the foundation of sustainable growth, 
operational excellence and stakeholder trust. Guided by robust oversight, ethical business 
practices, regulatory compliance and transparent decision-making, we continuously strengthen 
our governance framework to support long-term value creation and advance our ambition of 
becoming a leading global CRDMO partner.

=== page 110 ===
How the board provides oversight
The Board provides comprehensive oversight of Cohance Lifesciences’ integrated platform by monitoring 
performance across financial, operational, scientific, regulatory, sustainability and strategic dimensions. 
Through regular reviews, the Board evaluates growth initiatives, technology investments, quality and 
compliance performance, enterprise risks, ESG commitments and capital allocation decisions. Supported 
by experienced leadership teams and the External Advisory Board, it oversees the identification and 
management of material economic, environmental and social impacts and ensures that scientific 
innovation, manufacturing excellence, sustainability priorities and effective risk management remain 
aligned with the Company’s long-term value creation strategy.
The Board delegates day-to-day responsibility for managing these impacts to the Executive Leadership 
Team and senior functional leaders across business verticals and corporate functions. Progress against 
material priorities, key risks and significant matters is periodically reviewed by the Board and its 
Committees through established governance and reporting mechanisms.
Material concerns relating to ethics, compliance, regulatory matters, cybersecurity, operational incidents 
and other significant risks are escalated through established governance and reporting mechanisms and 
are periodically communicated to the Board and its Committees for review and oversight. During FY26, the 
Board and its Committees were regularly apprised of significant matters affecting the Company, including 
regulatory developments, business continuity considerations and enterprise risks.
How did the governance hold during the merger and leadership transition 
FY26 was a defining test of Cohance Lifesciences’ governance framework. The Company successfully 
navigated a transformative merger, leadership transitions at the Managing Director and executive levels, a 
significant revenue slowdown and a major regulatory challenge at the Nacharam facility. Throughout this 
period, governance remained focused on continuity, accountability and long-term value creation.
The Board ensured leadership stability through timely succession planning, strengthening the 
organisation with experienced industry leaders, including the appointment of a new Executive Chairman 
and Group CEO, alongside dedicated leadership across the Strategic Business Units. To enhance 
accountability, the Company adopted a three-SBU structure, providing clear ownership for operational and 
financial performance.
These actions demonstrated the resilience of Cohance’s governance framework, enabling the Company to 
manage near-term challenges while continuing to invest in innovation, sustainability, capability expansion 
and long-term growth.

Compliance and Ethics 
Cohance Lifesciences is committed to conducting business 
responsibly and ethically, respecting internationally 
recognised protecting the environment, maintaining safe and 
inclusive workplaces and upholding the highest standards of 
integrity throughout its value chain. The Company expects 
employees, suppliers and business partners to adhere to these 
principles and applicable laws and regulations.
The Company has established policies and procedures to 
identify, disclose and appropriately manage actual, potential 
and perceived conflicts of interest involving Directors, Key 
Managerial Personnel and employees. Directors are required 
to make periodic disclosures of interests and abstain from 
participating in discussions or decisions where a conflict 
exists, in accordance with applicable laws and the Company’s 
governance policies.
Employees and business partners may seek guidance on 
ethical dilemmas, policy interpretation and responsible 
business conduct through designated management channels, 
compliance representatives and the Human Resources 
function and may raise concerns through established 
grievance and escalation mechanisms, where appropriate.Embedding Policy Commitments
The Company embeds its policy commitments through 
governance frameworks, employee training programmes, 
periodic certifications, supplier engagement processes, 
internal controls, compliance monitoring and risk 
management systems. Mechanisms including whistle-blower 
channels, investigations and corrective action processes 
support implementation and remediation.
Processes to Remediate Negative Impacts
Cohance Lifesciences maintains mechanisms to identify, 
investigate and remediate adverse impacts arising from its 
operations or business relationships. Concerns may be raised 
through whistle-blower channels, management escalation 
processes and stakeholder grievance mechanisms. Corrective 
and preventive actions are implemented, responsibilities 
assigned and progress monitored by appropriate governance 
bodies to assess the effectiveness of remediation measures.
Responsible Tax Practices
Cohance Lifesciences is committed to conducting its tax

Supporting Policies and Mechanisms
Code of Conduct
Cohance Lifesciences is committed to conducting business 
with integrity, transparency and accountability. The Company’s 
Code of Conduct establishes the ethical standards and 
expected behaviours for Directors, employees and business 
partners, covering areas such as regulatory compliance, 
conflicts of interest, fair dealing, confidentiality, workplace 
conduct and responsible decision-making. Adherence to the 
Code is reinforced through periodic awareness programmes 
and mandatory acknowledgements.
Whistle-blower Policy
The Company maintains a robust Whistle-blower Policy that 
enables employees and stakeholders to report concerns 
relating to unethical conduct, fraud, regulatory violations, 
financial irregularities, or breaches of the Code of Conduct 
without fear of retaliation. The mechanism promotes 
transparency and accountability by ensuring that concerns 
are investigated independently, confidentially and in a timely 
manner under the oversight of the appropriate governance 
bodies.
Anti-Bribery and Anti-Corruption Framework
Cohance Lifesciences follows a zero-tolerance approach 
toward bribery, corruption and unethical business practices. 
The Company’s Anti-Bribery and Anti-Corruption framework 
provides clear guidance on gifts, hospitality, facilitation 
payments, third-party interactions and conflict-of-interest 
management. Supported by internal controls, employee 
awareness programmes and compliance monitoring, the 
framework helps ensure that all business activities are 
conducted in accordance with applicable laws, regulations and 
the highest standards of ethical conduct.The effectiveness of actions undertaken to manage ethics 
and anti-corruption matters is periodically reviewed through 
compliance monitoring, internal audits, investigation 
outcomes, training completion rates and stakeholder 
feedback. Learnings arising from these reviews are 
incorporated into policy updates, control enhancements 
and awareness programmes to continuously strengthen the 
Company’s governance framework.
Communication and Training on Anti-Corruption 
Policies and Procedures
Cohance periodically communicates its anti-corruption and 
anti-bribery policies to directors, employees and relevant 
business partners and conducts awareness and training 
programmes to reinforce ethical conduct and compliance 
expectations.
Incidents of non-compliance and violations: 
During FY26, the Company reported zero significant instances 
of non-compliance with laws and regulations. The Company 
received a Warning Letter from the US FDA in February 2026 in 
relation to its Nacharam formulations facility. Comprehensive 
remediation measures and corrective and preventive actions 
have been initiated, supported by external quality and 
compliance experts, to address the matters identified and 
strengthen the facility’s quality systems and controls.
Legal actions for anti-competitive behaviour, anti-trust and monopoly practices
Cohance Lifesciences is committed to fair competition and responsible business conduct and complies with applicable 
competition, anti-trust and monopoly laws across the jurisdictions in which it operates. During FY26, the Company did not record 
any significant legal actions relating to anti-competitive behaviour, anti-trust or monopoly practices.

ECONOMIC OVERVIEW
  
  Global Economy
During 2025 and into early 2026, the global economy 
demonstrated resilience amid a complex and evolving 
macroeconomic landscape, underpinned by steady 
growth momentum, ongoing structural shifts, declining 
inflation trends and divergent regional performances.
Moderate yet Sustained Global Growth
According to the International Monetary Fund’s World 
Economic Outlook Update, global real gross domestic 
product (GDP) growth for 2025 is held at approximately 
3.4%, a rate broadly consistent with medium-term 
trends and reflective of robust activity in key advanced 
and emerging economies. 
This performance was supported by a combination of 
technology-led investment, accommodative financial 
conditions, fiscal support measures and private sector 
adaptability, which together helped offset headwinds 
from trade policy shifts and geopolitical uncertainty. 
Inflation and Price Dynamics
Across 2025, global inflation continued its downward 
trajectory from the elevated levels seen in recent 
years. This reflected both easing commodity prices 
and the gradual adjustment of monetary policy in 
major economies, reinforcing headline disinflation and 
contributing to improved prospects for price stability. 
However, inflation convergence varied across regions, 
with advanced economies generally approaching 
central bank targets more rapidly than many emerging 
and developing economies.Regional Divergences and Structural Drivers
United States: Maintained solid expansion, driven by 
strong consumption and investment, supported by 
favourable labour market dynamics.
China: Continued to deliver meaningful growth, 
although structural rebalancing and shifts in external 
demand kept expansion moderate relative to prior 
decades.
Emerging and Developing Markets: Growth outcomes 
varied markedly across regions, with some economies 
benefiting from domestic demand resilience while 
others faced tighter financing conditions and structural 
constraints. 
Key Risks and Policy Considerations
The IMF highlighted several downside risks to the 
global outlook, including potential re-evaluation of 
technology investment expectations, heightened 
geopolitical tensions and shifts in global trade policies 
that could constrain cross-border flows and business 
confidence. 
In response, policymakers were advised to restore fiscal 
buffers, preserve price and financial stability, reduce 
uncertainty and implement structural reforms to 
support inclusive and sustainable growth.

Looking ahead, the global economy is expected to maintain 
a moderate growth trajectory. According to the IMF, global 
real GDP growth is projected to remain around 3.1% in 2026, 
reflecting underlying resilience despite ongoing structural and 
geopolitical challenges. However, global headline inflation is 
projected to rise modestly in 2026 before resuming its decline 
in 2027.
The outlook is supported by technology-led investments, 
improving financial conditions and gradual disinflation, which 
could provide central banks greater flexibility in calibrating monetary policy. At the same time, risks remain tilted to the 
downside, including potential trade disruptions, geopolitical 
tensions and financial market volatility.
Overall, the medium-term outlook signals measured expansion 
with cautious optimism, underscoring the need for prudent 
fiscal management, structural reforms and policy coordination 
to sustain stability and growth.

    Indian Economy
The Indian economy in FY26 demonstrated remarkable 
resilience, solidifying its position as the fastest-growing major 
economy. As per the Second Advance Estimates, the nation 
has successfully navigated global headwinds through robust 
domestic demand and strategic structural reforms.
GDP Growth and Primary Drivers
India’s real GDP growth for FY26 is estimated at 7.6%, 
exceeding initial projections, according to MoSPI. Growth 
was driven by sustained government capital expenditure, 
which rose 10% year-on-year, with infrastructure investments 
such as dedicated freight corridors and green energy grids 
crowding in private investment. Additionally, the maturation 
of Digital Public Infrastructure has enhanced formalisation 
and efficiency, contributing meaningfully to overall economic 
expansion.
Inflation and Private Consumption
Headline CPI inflation remained within the Reserve Bank of 
India’s target, averaging 3.2%–3.5% during FY26. The central 
bank implemented two repo rate cuts, supporting spending, 
investment and overall growth. Although seasonal food price 
volatility persisted, supply-side measures and a stable rupee 
helped contain imported inflation. Stable prices drove a 
strong recovery in private consumption, with urban demand 
leading, while rural consumption reached a four-year high in 
Q2 FY26, supported by better farm realisations and declining 
unemployment. 
Agriculture and Industrial Activity
The agricultural sector recorded healthy growth, supported by 
a well-distributed monsoon and the expansion of the “Agri-
Stack” digital initiative. Industrial activity was equally strong, 
with the manufacturing sector benefiting from the peak 
implementation of Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes. 
Output in electronics, semiconductors and renewable energy 
components grew in the double digits. The Purchasing 
Managers’ Index (PMI) consistently hovered around 58, 
indicating sustained expansionary momentum.External Trade and GST Collections
Despite a sluggish global recovery, India’s external trade 
reached an all-time high of US$ 863 billion, up from US$ 825 
billion in FY25. Services exports, particularly in high-end 
Global Capability Centres (GCCs), reached an estimated US$ 
421 billion, keeping the Current Account Deficit (CAD) at a 
manageable level of around 1.0%–1.2% of GDP . On the fiscal 
front, Goods and Services Tax (GST) collections demonstrated 
exceptional buoyancy. Gross collections for the full year 
reached ₹22.27 Lakh Crore, marking an 8.3% year-on-year 
growth, reflecting enhanced compliance and a broadened tax 
base following the latest digital audits.
Outlook for FY27 and Beyond
The outlook for FY27 remains cautiously optimistic, despite 
risks from oil price shocks, monsoon variability, supply chain 
disruptions and inflationary pressures. As India approaches 
the milestone of becoming the world’s third-largest economy, 
the focus is shifting toward “Viksit Bharat” goals. Thus, key 
priorities include accelerating the energy transition and 
deepening labour market reforms. While geopolitical risks 
remain a variable, India’s strong domestic macroeconomic 
fundamentals provide a stable cushion for sustainable long-
term growth.
 
  Why Is India’s Macro Environment Favourable? 
India’s resilient growth, strengthening manufacturing ecosystem 
and cost competitiveness create a favourable operating backdrop 
for manufacturing. Moreover, stable inflation improves cost 
visibility, while the “China+1” shift creates opportunities for 
qualified Indian manufacturers such as Cohance.
